text:
maria: Heads-up — our holiday promo sims (12/18-12/26) are showing a bursty pattern that could push tokens/sec ~+40% at peak. We should run a fast throughput vs GPU-hours plan and decide pre-warm / reserved vs spot strategy. :snowflake: 
ben: Do you have the request distribution? concurrent requests vs tokens/sec matters a lot for batching.
kai: I pulled a quick histogram from last year's same-week: avg tokens/request ~260, median 120, p95 ~1600, p99 ~4200. But this promo adds a heavy tail — simulated p99 ~8k tokens.
anya: If p99 goes to 8k, our per-request latency and KV cache behavior changes a lot. Need to factor in max sequence length for kernel selection.
evan: Also region constraint — APAC capacity is limited that week. We should model cross-region overflow (route to us-east fallback) and the network egress cost.
maria: Good points. For a quick triage, can someone run sensitivity sims for: (1) avg tokens +/-20%, (2) p95/p99 tails, (3) batching windows 10ms/40ms/100ms, (4) cache hit 0/50/80%? Aim for GPU-hours and expected p99 latency.
kai: Running small sim now. Command I'm using: ```bash python infra/sim/throughput_scan.py --qps 12k --avg-tokens 260 --p99-tokens 8000 --batch-windows 10,40,100 --cache-hit 0,50,80 --duration 9``` Will post numbers in a sec.
ben: Don't forget to toggle model-mix: mix of quantized L2 (cheap) vs FP16 L1 (expensive). The fallback policy matters if L2 runs out.
anya: Also include autoscaler cooldown and max scale rate (we can't add more than 200 GPUs in 15m in a region — operational limit).
evan: Cost note: using spot GPUs for overflow could save ~30% but reliability risk if we rely on them for the p99 tail. Prefer reserved/dedicated for steady baseline and spot for transient bursts + graceful fallback.
maria: Agree. Kai — add run with dedicated baseline + spot overflow (simulate 30% of burst on spot) and show 99th failure probability if spot reclaimed.
kai: Quick output (rough): batch 10ms: need 2.0k gpus baseline, GPU-hours ~432k over 9d. batch 40ms: 1.6k gpus baseline, GPU-hours ~345k. batch 100ms: 1.2k gpus, GPU-hours ~260k. With cache 80% these drop ~25%. p99 latency target (<=600ms) only met with batch windows >=40ms + cache>=50% in the sim.
eny: (typo) meant evan^^
ben: Those numbers are useful. Can you also break out tokens/sec per GPU and tokens/sec per active request? We need to translate to cost per 1M tokens for pricing impact.
kai: Sure — rough tokens/sec per GPU at 40ms batching = ~85k tokens/s/GPU at median model mix. With cost assumptions that maps to ~$0.12 per 1M tokens for dedicated baseline (varies by region).
anya: Two operational action items: 1) pre-warm reserved pool in us-east to cover 70% of expected peak (commit by 12/1), 2) schedule spot overflow + fast-fail fallback path for degraded models. I'll draft runbook.
maria: I'll sync with finance on the cost impact and get OK for reserved commit if numbers look like kai's. Also need telemetry hooks: per-route token histogram, batch size distribution, and spot reclaim alerts.
deploy-bot: Note: scheduled capacity change request created (#CR-842) — tentative add 600 dedicated GPUs to us-east on 2026-12-15 pending approval.
ben: Final ask: can we run a queued workload sim (bulk ingestion) too? Bulk jobs could saturate batching windows and starve low-latency traffic — consider token rate limiting and separate pools.
maria: Good call. Add queued bulk jobs as separate scenario (dedicated pool) and throttle policy. Thanks all — please drop sim outputs into the shared spreadsheet / channel thread.
